sentences.text: ?Court No. - 74
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 15231 of 2023

Applicant :- Mahesh Chausle @ Mahesh Chausel
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Ram Prasad Kanaujiya
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri R.P. Kanaujiya, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ghanshyam Mishra, learned Brief Holder for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 112 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Rail Bazar,
District Kanpur Nagar during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged on 28.05.2022 through an application under Section 156(3)
Cr.P.C. dated 21.06.2021 and according to the FIR the marriage of the applicant was performed with sister of the informant on 05.02.2015 and after marriage applicant and his family members started torturing his sister for want of Rs. 1 Lakh and on 09.05.2021 applicant and his family members called the informant and stated that his sister fell down and sustained head injury and due to the head injury his sister died on 13.05.2021.
It is further mentioned in the FIR that for want of dowry applicant and his family members committed murder of sister of the informant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and in fact deceased i.e. sister of the informant accidentally sustained injuries on her head due to fall and immediately after that she was admitted to the hospital and this fact has been admitted by the informant himself in the FIR and during treatment she died on 13.05.2021 and as per post mortem report of the deceased she died due to shock as she was in coma.
He further submits that as per medical certificate her cause of death was natural.

5. He further submits that admittedly deceased died during medical treatment in the hospital on 13.05.2021 and application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was moved on 21.06.2021 i.e. after about more than one month and this fact itself shows that entire allegations made against the applicant in the FIR are totally false and baseless.

He further submits that although on 13.05.2021 an application was moved by the informant to the police with regard to the death of her sister and in the application he although stated that due to the assault made by applicant and his family members deceased sustained internal injuries but as according to the medical certificate of the deceased,
cause of death was natural one, therefore, no FIR was lodged.
6.

He further submits that applicant neither demanded any dowry nor he ever harassed the deceased and he has been implicated in the present matter only due to the reason that he is husband of the deceased.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is the husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there was also demand of dowry.

He further submits that on the same day of death of his sister i.e. 13.05.2021 informant moved an application against applicant and his family members with the allegation that they made assault and due to that deceased sustained injuries and died but in spite of that his FIR could not be lodged thereafter he had to file an application under Section 156(3)
Cr.P.C., therefore, delay in filing the application after about more than one month is duly explained but could not dispute the fact that as per post mortem report deceased died due to shock while she was in coma and according to medical certificate issued by the hospital with regard to her death she died natural death.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
9. Although, applicant is husband and his wife died within seven years of marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also demand of dowry but from the post mortem it appears that deceased died due to shock while she was in coma and as per applicant she accidentally fell down and sustained head injury and thereafter she was admitted to the hospital and information of the accident has been given to the informant and informant also admitted this fact in the FIR and medical certificate of cause of death, which has been annexed along with post mortem report as Annexure-3 to the affidavit shows that she died due to the sudden cardio pulmonary arrest and manner of death was noted natural, therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case,
in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

sentences.text: Therefore, from the discussion made above, in view of this Court, it is a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
11. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant - Mahesh Chausle @ Mahesh Chausel be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
13. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
